name: _CData
doc: This non-public class is the common base class of all ctypes data types. Among other things, all ctypes type instances contain a memory block that hold C compatible data; the address of the memory block is returned by the addressof() helper function. Another instance variable is exposed as _objects; this contains other Python objects that need to be kept alive in case the memory block contains pointers.

name: __pointer_type__
doc: The pointer type that was created by calling POINTER() for corresponding ctypes data type. If a pointer type was not yet created, the attribute is missing.

name: _b_base_
doc: Sometimes ctypes data instances do not own the memory block they contain, instead they share part of the memory block of a base object. The _b_base_ read-only member is the root ctypes object that owns the memory block.

name: _b_needsfree_
doc: This read-only variable is true when the ctypes data instance has allocated the memory block itself, false otherwise.

name: _objects
doc: This member is either None or a dictionary containing Python objects that need to be kept alive so that the memory block contents is kept valid. This object is only exposed for debugging; never modify the contents of this dictionary.

name: from_address
doc: This method returns a ctypes type instance using the memory specified by address which must be an integer.

name: from_buffer
doc: This method returns a ctypes instance that shares the buffer of the source object. The source object must support the writeable buffer interface. The optional offset parameter specifies an offset into the source buffer in bytes; the default is zero. If the source buffer is not large enough a ValueError is raised.

name: from_buffer_copy
doc: This method creates a ctypes instance, copying the buffer from the source object buffer which must be readable. The optional offset parameter specifies an offset into the source buffer in bytes; the default is zero. If the source buffer is not large enough a ValueError is raised.

name: from_param
doc: This method adapts obj to a ctypes type. It is called with the actual object used in a foreign function call when the type is present in the foreign function’s argtypes tuple; it must return an object that can be used as a function call parameter.

name: in_dll
doc: This method returns a ctypes type instance exported by a shared library. name is the name of the symbol that exports the data, library is the loaded shared library.

name: _CFuncPtr
doc: Function Pointer

name: argtypes
doc: specify the argument types

name: errcheck
doc: a function to check for errors

name: restype
doc: specify the result type

name: _Pointer
doc:
Private, abstract base class for pointers.

Concrete pointer types are created by calling POINTER() with the type that will be pointed to; this is done automatically by pointer().

If a pointer points to an array, its elements can be read and written using standard subscript and slice accesses. Pointer objects have no size, so len() will raise TypeError. Negative subscripts will read from the memory before the pointer (as in C), and out-of-range subscripts will probably crash with an access violation (if you’re lucky).

name: _type_
doc: Specifies the type pointed to.

name: contents
doc: the object this pointer points to (read-write)

name: _SimpleCData
doc:
This non-public class is the base class of all fundamental ctypes data types.
It contains the common attributes of the fundamental ctypes data types.
_SimpleCData is a subclass of _CData, so it inherits their methods and attributes.

name: _type_
doc: Class attribute that contains an internal type code, as a single-character string. See Fundamental data types for a summary.

name: value
doc: This attribute contains the actual value of the instance. For integer and pointer types, it is an integer, for character types, it is a single character bytes object or string, for character pointer types it is a Python bytes object or string.

name: addressof
doc: Return the address of the C instance internal buffer

name: alignment
doc:
alignment(C type) -> integer
alignment(C instance) -> integer
Return the alignment requirements of a C instance

name: ArgumentError
doc: This exception is raised when a foreign function call cannot convert one of the passed arguments.

name: ARRAY
doc: Create an array. Equivalent to type * length, where type is a ctypes data type and length an integer.

changed.text: Soft deprecated. In favor of multiplication.

name: Array
doc:
Abstract base class for arrays.

The recommended way to create concrete array types is by multiplying any
ctypes data type with a non-negative integer. Alternatively, you can subclass
this type and define _length_ and _type_ class variables. Array elements can
be read and written using standard subscript and slice accesses for slice
reads, the resulting object is not itself an Array.

name: _length_
doc: A positive integer specifying the number of elements in the array. Out-of-range subscripts result in an IndexError. Will be returned by len().

name: _type_
doc: Specifies the type of each element in the array.

name: BigEndianStructure
doc: Structure with big endian byte order

name: BigEndianUnion
doc: Union with big endian byte order

name: byref
doc: Return a pointer lookalike to a C instance, only usable as function argument.

name: c_bool
doc: Represent the C bool datatype (more accurately, _Bool from C99). Its value can be True or False, and the constructor accepts any object that has a truth value.

name: c_byte
doc: Represents the C signed char datatype, and interprets the value as small integer. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done.

name: c_char
doc: Represents the C char datatype, and interprets the value as a single character. The constructor accepts an optional string initializer, the length of the string must be exactly one character.

name: c_char_p
doc: Represents the C char* datatype when it points to a zero-terminated string. For a general character pointer that may also point to binary data, POINTER(c_char) must be used. The constructor accepts an integer address, or a bytes object.

name: c_double
doc: Represents the C double datatype. The constructor accepts an optional float initializer.

name: c_double_complex
doc: Represents the C double complex datatype, if available. The constructor accepts an optional complex initializer.

name: c_float
doc: Represents the C float datatype. The constructor accepts an optional float initializer.

name: c_float_complex
doc: Represents the C float complex datatype, if available. The constructor accepts an optional complex initializer.

name: c_int
doc: Represents the C signed int datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done. On platforms where sizeof(int) == sizeof(long) it is an alias to c_long.

name: c_int16
doc: Represents the C 16-bit signed int datatype. Usually an alias for c_short.

name: c_int32
doc: Represents the C 32-bit signed int datatype. Usually an alias for c_int.

name: c_int64
doc: Represents the C 64-bit signed int datatype. Usually an alias for c_longlong.

name: c_int8
doc: Represents the C 8-bit signed int datatype. It is an alias for c_byte.

name: c_long
doc: Represents the C signed long datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done.

name: c_longdouble
doc: Represents the C long double datatype. The constructor accepts an optional float initializer. On platforms where sizeof(long double) == sizeof(double) it is an alias to c_double.

name: c_longdouble_complex
doc: Represents the C long double complex datatype, if available. The constructor accepts an optional complex initializer.

name: c_longlong
doc: Represents the C signed long long datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done. On platforms where sizeof(long long) == sizeof(long) it is an alias to c_long.

name: c_short
doc: Represents the C signed short datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done.

name: c_size_t
doc: Represents the C size_t datatype. Usually an alias for another unsigned integer type.

name: c_ssize_t
doc: Represents the Py_ssize_t datatype. This is a signed version of size_t; that is, the POSIX ssize_t type. Usually an alias for another integer type.

name: c_time_t
doc: Represents the C time_t datatype. Usually an alias for another integer type.

name: c_ubyte
doc: Represents the C unsigned char datatype, it interprets the value as small integer. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done.

name: c_uint
doc: Represents the C unsigned int datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done. On platforms where sizeof(int) == sizeof(long) it is an alias for c_ulong.

name: c_uint16
doc: Represents the C 16-bit unsigned int datatype. Usually an alias for c_ushort.

name: c_uint32
doc: Represents the C 32-bit unsigned int datatype. Usually an alias for c_uint.

name: c_uint64
doc: Represents the C 64-bit unsigned int datatype. Usually an alias for c_ulonglong.

name: c_uint8
doc: Represents the C 8-bit unsigned int datatype. It is an alias for c_ubyte.

name: c_ulong
doc: Represents the C unsigned long datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done.

name: c_ulonglong
doc: Represents the C unsigned long long datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done. On platforms where sizeof(long long) == sizeof(long) it is an alias to c_long.

name: c_ushort
doc: Represents the C unsigned short datatype. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer; no overflow checking is done.

name: c_void_p
doc: Represents the C void* type. The value is represented as integer. The constructor accepts an optional integer initializer.

name: c_wchar
doc: Represents the C wchar_t datatype, and interprets the value as a single character unicode string. The constructor accepts an optional string initializer, the length of the string must be exactly one character.

name: c_wchar_p
doc: Represents the C wchar_t* datatype, which must be a pointer to a zero-terminated wide character string. The constructor accepts an integer address, or a string.

name: cast
doc: This function is similar to the cast operator in C. It returns a new instance of type which points to the same memory block as obj. type must be a pointer type, and obj must be an object that can be interpreted as a pointer.

name: CDLL
signatures: CDLL(name, mode=DEFAULT_MODE, handle=None, use_errno=False, use_last_error=False, winmode=None)
doc:
An instance of this class represents a loaded dll/shared
library, exporting functions using the standard C calling
convention (named 'cdecl' on Windows).

The exported functions can be accessed as attributes, or by
indexing with the function name.  Examples:

<obj>.qsort -> callable object
<obj>['qsort'] -> callable object

Calling the functions releases the Python GIL during the call and
reacquires it afterwards.

changed.text: The name parameter can now be a path-like object.

name: cdll
doc: Creates CDLL instances.

name: _handle
doc: The system handle used to access the library.

name: _name
doc: The name of the library passed in the constructor.

name: CField
doc: Structure/Union member

name: bit_offset
doc: additional offset in bits (relative to byte_offset); zero for non-bitfields

name: bit_size
doc: size of this field in bits

name: byte_offset
doc: offset in bytes of this field. For bitfields: excludes bit_offset.

name: byte_size
doc: size of this field in bytes

name: is_anonymous
doc: true if this field is anonymous

name: is_bitfield
doc: true if this is a bitfield

name: name
doc: name of this field

name: offset
doc: offset in bytes of this field (same as byte_offset)

name: size
doc: size in bytes of this field. For bitfields, this is a legacy packed value; use byte_size instead

name: type
doc: type of this field

name: CFUNCTYPE
doc:
CFUNCTYPE(restype, *argtypes,
             use_errno=False, use_last_error=False) -> function prototype.

restype: the result type
argtypes: a sequence specifying the argument types

The function prototype can be called in different ways to create a
callable object:

prototype(integer address) -> foreign function
prototype(callable) -> create and return a C callable function from callable
prototype(integer index, method name[, paramflags]) -> foreign function calling a COM method
prototype((ordinal number, dll object)[, paramflags]) -> foreign function exported by ordinal
prototype((function name, dll object)[, paramflags]) -> foreign function exported by name

name: COMError
doc: This exception is raised when a COM method call failed.

name: details
doc: The 5-tuple (descr, source, helpfile, helpcontext, progid).

name: hresult
doc: The integer value representing the error code.

name: text
doc: The error message.

name: CopyComPointer
doc: Copies a COM pointer from src to dst and returns the Windows specific HRESULT value.

name: create_string_buffer
doc:
create_string_buffer(aBytes) -> character array
create_string_buffer(anInteger) -> character array
create_string_buffer(aBytes, anInteger) -> character array

name: create_unicode_buffer
doc:
create_unicode_buffer(aString) -> character array
create_unicode_buffer(anInteger) -> character array
create_unicode_buffer(aString, anInteger) -> character array

name: DEFAULT_MODE
doc: The default mode which is used to load shared libraries. On OSX 10.3, this is RTLD_GLOBAL, otherwise it is the same as RTLD_LOCAL.

name: DllCanUnloadNow
doc: This function is a hook which allows implementing in-process COM servers with ctypes. It is called from the DllCanUnloadNow function that the _ctypes extension dll exports.

name: DllGetClassObject
doc: This function is a hook which allows implementing in-process COM servers with ctypes. It is called from the DllGetClassObject function that the _ctypes extension dll exports.

name: FormatError
doc: Returns a textual description of the error code code. If no error code is specified, the last error code is used by calling the Windows API function GetLastError().

name: get_errno
doc: Returns the current value of the ctypes-private copy of the system errno variable in the calling thread.

name: get_last_error
doc: Returns the current value of the ctypes-private copy of the system LastError variable in the calling thread.

name: GetLastError
doc: Returns the last error code set by Windows in the calling thread. This function calls the Windows GetLastError() function directly, it does not return the ctypes-private copy of the error code.

name: HRESULT
doc: Represents a HRESULT value, which contains success or error information for a function or method call.

name: LibraryLoader
doc: Class which loads shared libraries. dlltype should be one of the CDLL, PyDLL, WinDLL, or OleDLL types.

name: LoadLibrary
doc: Load a shared library into the process and return it. This method always returns a new instance of the library.

name: LittleEndianStructure
doc: Structure base class

name: LittleEndianUnion
doc: Union base class

name: memmove
doc: Same as the standard C memmove library function: copies count bytes from src to dst. dst and src must be integers or ctypes instances that can be converted to pointers.

name: memoryview_at
doc:
memoryview_at(ptr, size[, readonly]) -> memoryview

Return a memoryview representing the memory at void *ptr.

name: memset
doc: Same as the standard C memset library function: fills the memory block at address dst with count bytes of value c. dst must be an integer specifying an address, or a ctypes instance.

name: OleDLL
doc: See CDLL, the superclass, for common information.

changed.text: WindowsError used to be raised, which is now an alias of OSError.

name: oledll
doc: Creates OleDLL instances.

name: POINTER
doc:
Create and return a new ctypes pointer type.

Pointer types are cached and reused internally,
so calling this function repeatedly is cheap.

name: pointer
doc:
Create a new pointer instance, pointing to 'obj'.

The returned object is of the type POINTER(type(obj)). Note that if you
just want to pass a pointer to an object to a foreign function call, you
should use byref(obj) which is much faster.

name: py_object
doc: Represents the C PyObject* datatype. Calling this without an argument creates a NULL PyObject* pointer.

changed.text: py_object is now a generic type.

name: PyDLL
signatures: PyDLL(name, mode=4, handle=None, use_errno=False, use_last_error=False, winmode=None)
doc:
This class represents the Python library itself.  It allows
accessing Python API functions.  The GIL is not released, and
Python exceptions are handled correctly.

name: pydll
doc: Creates PyDLL instances.

name: PYFUNCTYPE
doc: The returned function prototype creates functions that use the Python calling convention. Unlike CFUNCTYPE() and WINFUNCTYPE(), ctypes does not release the GIL before calling the foreign function, so the function may safely use the Python C API. Note that this does not prevent the GIL from being released during the call.

name: pythonapi
doc: An instance of PyDLL that exposes Python C API functions as attributes. Note that all these functions are assumed to return C int, which is of course not always the truth, so you have to assign the correct restype attribute to use these functions.

name: resize
doc: This function resizes the internal memory buffer of obj, which must be an instance of a ctypes type. It is not possible to make the buffer smaller than the native size of the objects type, as given by sizeof(type(obj)), but it is possible to enlarge the buffer.

name: RTLD_GLOBAL
doc: Flag to use as mode parameter. On platforms where this flag is not available, it is defined as the integer zero.

name: RTLD_LOCAL
doc: Flag to use as mode parameter. On platforms where this is not available, it is the same as RTLD_GLOBAL.

name: set_errno
doc: Set the current value of the ctypes-private copy of the system errno variable in the calling thread to value and return the previous value.

name: set_last_error
doc: Sets the current value of the ctypes-private copy of the system LastError variable in the calling thread to value and return the previous value.

name: sizeof
doc: Return the size in bytes of a C instance.

name: string_at
doc:
string_at(ptr[, size]) -> string

Return the byte string at void *ptr.

name: Structure
doc: Structure base class

name: _align_
doc: An optional small integer that allows increasing the alignment of the structure when being packed or unpacked to/from memory.

name: _anonymous_
doc: An optional sequence that lists the names of unnamed (anonymous) fields. _anonymous_ must be already defined when _fields_ is assigned, otherwise it will have no effect.

name: _fields_
doc: A sequence defining the structure fields. The items must be 2-tuples or 3-tuples. The first item is the name of the field, the second item specifies the type of the field; it can be any ctypes data type.

name: _layout_
doc: An optional string naming the struct/union layout. It can currently be set to:

name: _pack_
doc: An optional small integer that allows overriding the alignment of structure fields in the instance.

deprecated.text: For historical reasons, if _pack_ is non-zero, the MSVC-compatible layout will be used by default. On non-Windows platforms, this default is deprecated and is slated to become an error in Python 3.19. If it is intended, set _layout_ to 'ms' explicitly.

name: Union
doc: Union base class

name: dllist
doc: Return a list of loaded shared libraries in the current process.

name: find_library
doc: Try to find a library and return a pathname.

changed.text: Soft deprecated. This function is kept for use in cases where it works, but not expected to be updated for additional platforms and configurations.

name: find_msvcrt
doc: Returns the filename of the VC runtime library used by Python, and by the extension modules.

name: WinDLL
doc: See CDLL, the superclass, for common information.

name: windll
doc: Creates WinDLL instances.

name: WinError
doc: Creates an instance of OSError. If code is not specified, GetLastError() is called to determine the error code. If descr is not specified, FormatError() is called to get a textual description of the error.

changed.text: An instance of WindowsError used to be created, which is now an alias of OSError.

name: WINFUNCTYPE
doc: The returned function prototype creates functions that use the stdcall calling convention. The function will release the GIL during the call. use_errno and use_last_error have the same meaning as above.

name: wstring_at
doc:
wstring_at(ptr[, size]) -> string

Return the wide-character string at void *ptr.
